doc.title: Bob Cranshaw interviewed by Michael Woods, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995

title: Why bass: a drummer father, family of musicians, and football
summary: Cranshaw wanted to be a percussionist but his father was a drummer and brothers played piano and vibes, so he took up bass around 1949-50; choir music and football also figure.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Yeah. You are an outstanding bass player. And you’ve been on just a scad of recordings. But how did you get started? First of all what attracted you to the bass as to other instruments.

I’m really a percussionist. I started out wanting to be a concert percussionist. I was not really interested in jazz at all but I wanted to be a classical percussionist. But my father was a drummer who grew up with Count Basie, grew up in Kansas City, so he goes back to the Count Basie early days, and I have a brother who is a pianist who is also in New York and worked briefly with Miles years ago. And I have a brother who is a vibist. So since my father was also a drummer, I figured there was no reason for me to buck — I just wanted to play anything. I wanted to play with the family. And since he was a drummer, I wasn’t going to move him over, he was there first. So I decided to play bass. And I liked choral music a lot. And in school and in high school and in college I was always involved in choirs and I wanted to kind of be a choir director. And my father was a choir director for the church so I got a chance, I was always around music and I just decided to play bass. So my brother would sit down at the piano and I guess this was in say maybe ‘49 or ‘50, I started to study the bass. And I really had a hard time trying to learn the instrument. I mean it wasn’t really easy. But I wanted to play football. I was also a football player, and I was more interested. You know I wasn’t sure whether I liked bass or what was happening.
